argument: The removal must be carried by the wet stroke's thinning and return, not by a clay-coloured ring laid over an unchanged path.
A caption-free comparison should find the same gathering, pale mouth, and thinner return with the basin witnesses hidden; if only the dark wells speak, the rule has failed.
Pointer and Enter/Space must create the same bounded removal, while lifting the latest basin must restore the exact prior route and pigment state.
A drain is an attractive metaphor. Delete v004 if the rings explain more than the changed body of the wet marks, or if the field reads as a diagram of sinks.
